refuse a house whose center stands more than WEB_REACH_FT deep in the union of the web's hard ground (envelope, crops, toe, wet) inflated by WEB_HARD_GAP; FR-005 answered for seats unreachable by construction, the rest left to the roll's self-report
decisions.why: The round-1 form. Against the GM's purpose (the same exercise: make it faster, maps may shift while settlements stay what they are) and FR-005 (refuse a seat the reach rule would fail), refusing a SUBSET of those seats is legitimate where general seat-time reach prediction is recorded as failed (driver.py; wrong on five of six seeds), and it is recorded with that reason. Checked in code: web lanes keep WEB_HARD_GAP off `hard` (web.py 478/517, route.py 111, serve.py 130/419, clearance.py 32), skeleton arms clip 20 off it (web.py 125), the spur tip stops SPUR_SETBACK=17 out of the envelope (track.py spur_path) and the connector is route_around the envelope at 17 (track.py 405/524). One premise is not exact: connector_track keeps the LEAST-BAD bearing over crops and wet ground (clearance.py 302), so a connector can stand inside the crop/toe/wet part of the union. A refusal is then wrong only if that connector passes within 100 ft of a house more than 100 ft deep in the union, which the placer's own hard ground (plots, marshes, toe already refused for the house) makes rare, and SC-013 (no fewer houses, cohort, rescue scenario, toys) bounds the outcome. Not blocking; the implementation should MEASURE the premise (no drawn way point inside the union on the pool and the 24-seed cohort) rather than assert it.
